WITH target_parts AS (
    SELECT p_partkey, p_mfgr
    FROM part
    WHERE p_size = 6
      AND p_type LIKE '%NICKEL'
),
europe_suppliers AS (
    SELECT s.s_suppkey, s.s_name, s.s_address, s.s_phone, s.s_acctbal, s.s_comment, n.n_name
    FROM supplier s
    JOIN nation n ON s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
    JOIN region r ON n.n_regionkey = r.r_regionkey
    WHERE r.r_name = 'EUROPE'
),
min_supplycost AS (
    SELECT ps.ps_partkey, MIN(ps.ps_supplycost) AS min_supplycost
    FROM partsupp ps
    JOIN target_parts tp ON ps.ps_partkey = tp.p_partkey
    JOIN europe_suppliers es ON ps.ps_suppkey = es.s_suppkey
    GROUP BY ps.ps_partkey
)
SELECT es.s_acctbal, es.s_name, es.n_name, tp.p_partkey, tp.p_mfgr,
       es.s_address, es.s_phone, es.s_comment
FROM target_parts tp
JOIN min_supplycost msc ON tp.p_partkey = msc.ps_partkey
JOIN partsupp ps ON ps.ps_partkey = msc.ps_partkey
                AND ps.ps_supplycost = msc.min_supplycost
JOIN europe_suppliers es ON ps.ps_suppkey = es.s_suppkey
ORDER BY es.s_acctbal DESC, es.n_name, es.s_name, tp.p_partkey
LIMIT 100;

Preserve tie semantics: join back to partsupp on the computed minimum cost and filter to European suppliers, so all suppliers achieving the minimum cost per part are returned exactly as in the original query.

    FROM supplier s
    JOIN nation n ON s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
    JOIN region r ON n.n_regionkey = r.r_regionkey
    WHERE r.r_name = 'ASIA'
),
filtered_part AS (
    SELECT p_partkey, p_mfgr
    FROM part
    WHERE p_size = 46
      AND p_type LIKE '%NICKEL'
),
min_asia_cost AS (
    SELECT ps.ps_partkey, MIN(ps.ps_supplycost) AS min_ps_supplycost
    FROM partsupp ps
    JOIN filtered_part fp ON ps.ps_partkey = fp.p_partkey
    JOIN asia_supplier asup ON ps.ps_suppkey = asup.s_suppkey

FROM filtered_part fp
JOIN min_asia_cost m ON fp.p_partkey = m.ps_partkey
JOIN partsupp ps ON m.ps_partkey = ps.ps_partkey AND m.min_ps_supplycost = ps.ps_supplycost
JOIN asia_supplier asup ON ps.ps_suppkey = asup.s_suppkey

WITH eligible_parts AS (
    SELECT p.p_partkey, p.p_mfgr
    FROM part p
    WHERE p.p_size = 3
      AND p.p_type LIKE '%NICKEL'
),
min_cost AS (
    SELECT ps.ps_partkey,
           MIN(ps.ps_supplycost) AS min_ps_supplycost
    FROM eligible_parts ep
    JOIN partsupp ps ON ps.ps_partkey = ep.p_partkey
    JOIN supplier s ON s.s_suppkey = ps.ps_suppkey
    JOIN nation n ON n.n_nationkey = s.s_nationkey
    JOIN region r ON r.r_regionkey = n.n_regionkey
    WHERE r.r_name = 'AMERICA'

       n.n_name,
       p.p_partkey,
       p.p_mfgr,
       s.s_address,
       s.s_phone,
       s.s_comment
FROM eligible_parts p
JOIN min_cost mc
  ON mc.ps_partkey = p.p_partkey
JOIN partsupp ps
  ON ps.ps_partkey = p.p_partkey
 AND ps.ps_supplycost = mc.min_ps_supplycost
JOIN supplier s
  ON s.s_suppkey = ps.ps_suppkey
JOIN nation n
  ON n.n_nationkey = s.s_nationkey
JOIN region r
  ON r.r_regionkey = n.n_regionkey
WHERE r.r_name = 'AMERICA'
ORDER BY s.s_acctbal DESC, n.n_name, s.s_name, p.p_partkey
LIMIT 100;

original_query: select sum(l_extendedprice) / 7.0 as avg_yearly from lineitem, part where p_partkey = l_partkey and p_brand = 'Brand#35' and p_container = 'LG PKG' and l_quantity < ( select 0.2 * avg(l_quantity) from lineitem where l_partkey = p_partkey );

SELECT SUM(l.l_extendedprice) / 7.0 AS avg_yearly
FROM part AS p
JOIN lineitem AS l ON l.l_partkey = p.p_partkey
JOIN (
    SELECT l_partkey, 0.2 * AVG(l_quantity) AS avg_quantity
    FROM lineitem
    GROUP BY l_partkey
) AS a ON a.l_partkey = l.l_partkey
WHERE p.p_brand = 'Brand#35'
  AND p.p_container = 'LG PKG'
  AND l.l_quantity < a.avg_quantity;

It can be replaced by a single pre-aggregated per-part average (derived table with GROUP BY or window function), which computes each part's average only once and eliminates the SubPlan executed repeatedly.
Rewrite the implicit comma join (`FROM lineitem, part WHERE ...`) as an explicit `JOIN ... ON`, improving readability and enabling cleaner join-order/predicate pushdown by the optimizer.
Keep the highly selective predicates `p_brand = 'Brand#35' AND p_container = 'LG PKG'` as early filters on part (only ~2K rows of 2M), so the lineitem side only needs rows for matching parts.

original_query: select sum(l_extendedprice) / 7.0 as avg_yearly from lineitem, part where p_partkey = l_partkey and p_brand = 'Brand#32' and p_container = 'WRAP PKG' and l_quantity < ( select 0.2 * avg(l_quantity) from lineitem where l_partkey = p_partkey );

FROM (

    WHERE p.p_brand = 'Brand#32'
      AND p.p_container = 'WRAP PKG'

WHERE li.l_quantity < li.avg_quantity_threshold;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated scalar subquery (0.2 * AVG(l_quantity) per p_partkey) with a window function AVG(l_quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY l_partkey), computed once after filtering to matching parts instead of re-scanning lineitem per row.

Push the selective part predicates (p_brand = 'Brand#32' AND p_container = 'WRAP PKG') into the inner subquery/join so the average is computed only for the ~0.1% matching part keys, reducing the window input from millions of rows to roughly tens of thousands.

Convert the comma join with join filter into an explicit inner JOIN between lineitem and part before the window computation, allowing a hash join with the small filtered part set to prune lineitem early.

Compute the threshold (0.2 * AVG) in the inner query and apply the quantity comparison in the outer query, ensuring the average is taken over all lineitem rows of each matching part (not only qualifying rows), preserving exact equivalence.

WITH order_qty AS (

    FROM lineitem
    GROUP BY l_orderkey

)

FROM lineitem AS l

Factor the predicates repeated in every OR branch (l_shipmode IN ('AIR','AIR REG') and l_shipinstruct = 'DELIVER IN PERSON') out of the OR expression, and fold constant arithmetic such as 10 + 10 into BETWEEN bounds (10-20, 19-29, 27-37). The plan's dominant cost is the parallel sequential scan of lineitem (60M rows) plus a complex OR join filter. A UNION ALL split of the three brand branches can enable branch-specific index access, but risks three lineitem scans when no suitable index exists, so it is not chosen as the default rewrite. Supporting indexes (e.g., lineitem(l_partkey, l_shipmode, l_shipinstruct, l_quantity) INCLUDE (l_extendedprice, l_discount) and part(p_brand, p_container, p_size) INCLUDE (p_partkey)) would have the highest impact (score ~9/10).

original_query: select s_name, s_address from supplier, nation where s_suppkey in ( select ps_suppkey from partsupp where ps_partkey in ( select p_partkey from part where p_name like 'burnished%' ) and ps_availqty > ( select 0.5 * sum(l_quantity) from lineitem where l_partkey = ps_partkey and l_suppkey = ps_suppkey and l_shipdate >= date '1996-01-01' and l_shipdate < date '1996-01-01' + interval '1' year ) ) and s_nationkey = n_nationkey and n_name = 'GERMANY' order by s_name;
rewritten_query:
WITH lineitem_totals AS (
    SELECT l.l_partkey, l.l_suppkey, 0.5 * SUM(l.l_quantity) AS half_sum
    FROM lineitem l
    WHERE l.l_shipdate >= DATE '1996-01-01'
      AND l.l_shipdate < DATE '1997-01-01'
      AND l.l_partkey IN (
          SELECT p_partkey
          FROM part
          WHERE p_name LIKE 'burnished%'
      )
    GROUP BY l.l_partkey, l.l_suppkey
)
SELECT s.s_name, s.s_address
FROM supplier s
JOIN nation n ON s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
WHERE n.n_name = 'GERMANY'
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM partsupp ps
      JOIN lineitem_totals lt
        ON lt.l_partkey = ps.ps_partkey
       AND lt.l_suppkey = ps.ps_suppkey
      WHERE ps.ps_suppkey = s.s_suppkey
        AND ps.ps_availqty > lt.half_sum
  )
ORDER BY s.s_name;

NULL semantics are preserved: parts with no lineitem rows in the window are excluded.
Replace the nested IN subqueries with an EXISTS-based semi-join against a qualifying_partsupp set, avoiding duplicate elimination and enabling early termination per supplier.
Constant-fold the date expression: replace `date '1996-01-01' + interval '1' year` with the equivalent constant `DATE '1997-01-01'`, making the range predicate directly sargable.

Convert the implicit comma join between supplier and nation into an explicit JOIN with the `n_name = 'GERMANY'` filter applied early, reducing the supplier set (nation has only 25 rows, so this is cheap and highly selective).
Pre-filter parts by `p_name LIKE 'burnished%'` before the lineitem aggregation to shrink the aggregated row set (part is 2M rows, the LIKE prefix is selective in TPC-H distributions).

WITH lineitem_sums AS (

    FROM lineitem
    WHERE l_shipdate >= DATE '1997-01-01'
      AND l_shipdate < DATE '1997-01-01' + INTERVAL '1' YEAR
    GROUP BY l_partkey, l_suppkey

SELECT s.s_name, s.s_address
FROM supplier s
JOIN nation n ON s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
WHERE n.n_name = 'KENYA'
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM partsupp ps
      JOIN part p ON p.p_partkey = ps.ps_partkey

This eliminates the per-partsupp SubPlan that repeatedly scanned lineitem (the dominant cost in the original plan).
Replace the nested IN subqueries with an EXISTS correlated to the outer supplier and explicit ANSI JOINs, allowing better join ordering and early termination once a qualifying partsupp row is found.
Push the selective filters (n_name = 'KENYA' and p_name LIKE 'spring%') so they are applied early in the plan, reducing candidate partsupp rows before the quantity comparison.

original_query: select s_name, s_address from supplier, nation where s_suppkey in ( select ps_suppkey from partsupp where ps_partkey in ( select p_partkey from part where p_name like 'burlywood%' ) and ps_availqty > ( select 0.5 * sum(l_quantity) from lineitem where l_partkey = ps_partkey and l_suppkey = ps_suppkey and l_shipdate >= date '1994-01-01' and l_shipdate < date '1994-01-01' + interval '1' year ) ) and s_nationkey = n_nationkey and n_name = 'ETHIOPIA' order by s_name;
rewritten_query:
WITH lineitem_agg AS (
    SELECT l_partkey, l_suppkey, SUM(l_quantity) AS sum_qty
    FROM lineitem
    WHERE l_shipdate >= DATE '1994-01-01'
      AND l_shipdate <  DATE '1995-01-01'
    GROUP BY l_partkey, l_suppkey
)
SELECT s.s_name, s.s_address
FROM supplier s
JOIN nation n
  ON n.n_nationkey = s.s_nationkey
WHERE n.n_name = 'ETHIOPIA'
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM partsupp ps
      JOIN part p
        ON p.p_partkey = ps.ps_partkey
      JOIN lineitem_agg la
        ON la.l_partkey = ps.ps_partkey
       AND la.l_suppkey = ps.ps_suppkey
      WHERE ps.ps_suppkey = s.s_suppkey
        AND p.p_name LIKE 'burlywood%'
        AND ps.ps_availqty > 0.5 * la.sum_qty

ORDER BY s.s_name;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Decorrelate the correlated aggregate subquery on lineitem into a grouped CTE `lineitem_agg` computed once (SUM(l_quantity) by l_partkey, l_suppkey for 1994), then join it to partsupp. This eliminates the per-row SubPlan that repeatedly scanned lineitem (the dominant cost in the original plan).

Replace the nested `IN` subqueries with explicit joins inside an EXISTS semi-join. This preserves the one-row-per-supplier semantics of the original `IN` predicate while allowing hash/semi-join execution.
Convert the implicit comma join between supplier and nation into an explicit JOIN with n_name = 'ETHIOPIA' as a filter, enabling the planner to filter suppliers early before the EXISTS semi-join.

original_query: select s_name, count(*) as numwait from supplier, lineitem l1, orders, nation where s_suppkey = l1.l_suppkey and o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and o_orderstatus = 'F' and l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate and exists ( select * from lineitem l2 where l2.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and l2.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey ) and not exists ( select * from lineitem l3 where l3.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and l3.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey and l3.l_receiptdate > l3.l_commitdate ) and s_nationkey = n_nationkey and n_name = 'MOZAMBIQUE' group by s_name order by numwait desc, s_name limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH candidate_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l1.l_orderkey
    FROM nation n
    JOIN supplier s ON s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
    JOIN lineitem l1 ON l1.l_suppkey = s.s_suppkey
    JOIN orders o ON o.o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey
    WHERE n.n_name = 'MOZAMBIQUE'
      AND o.o_orderstatus = 'F'
      AND l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate
),
order_stats AS (
    SELECT
        l.l_orderkey,
        COUNT(DISTINCT l.l_suppkey) AS supplier_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT l.l_suppkey) FILTER (WHERE l.l_receiptdate > l.l_commitdate) AS late_supplier_count,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE l.l_receiptdate > l.l_commitdate) AS late_line_count,
        MAX(l.l_suppkey) FILTER (WHERE l.l_receiptdate > l.l_commitdate) AS late_suppkey
    FROM lineitem l
    JOIN candidate_orders c ON c.l_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
    GROUP BY l.l_orderkey
)
SELECT
    s.s_name,
    SUM(os.late_line_count) AS numwait
FROM order_stats os
JOIN supplier s ON s.s_suppkey = os.late_suppkey
WHERE os.supplier_count > 1
  AND os.late_supplier_count = 1
GROUP BY s.s_name
ORDER BY numwait DESC, s.s_name
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Eliminate correlated EXISTS and NOT EXISTS subqueries on lineitem. Their semantics (order has >1 supplier and no other supplier with a late line) are replaced by per-order aggregation: supplier_count > 1 and late_supplier_count = 1. This removes the full parallel seq scan of lineitem l3 (anti-join) and per-row index probes into l2.

Early filtering: only orders containing a late lineitem from a MOZAMBIQUE supplier with o_orderstatus = 'F' can possibly qualify. These are pre-computed in candidate_orders, drastically reducing the rows the per-order aggregation must touch (nation selectivity ~1/25, late-line selectivity ~1/6).

Use conditional aggregation (COUNT(DISTINCT) FILTER, COUNT(*) FILTER, MAX() FILTER) to compute supplier_count, late_supplier_count, late_line_count and late_suppkey in one pass per candidate order. Since exactly one late supplier exists, all late lines in the order belong to it, so MAX(l_suppkey) FILTER identifies it and COUNT(*) FILTER counts its late lines — preserving exact equivalence with the original count(*).

Convert implicit comma joins to explicit ANSI JOINs and drive candidate_orders from the highly selective nation filter. The final join drops the redundant nation re-check: candidate_orders guarantees the unique late supplier is a MOZAMBIQUE supplier.

original_query: select s_name, count(*) as numwait from supplier, lineitem l1, orders, nation where s_suppkey = l1.l_suppkey and o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and o_orderstatus = 'F' and l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate and exists ( select * from lineitem l2 where l2.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and l2.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey ) and not exists ( select * from lineitem l3 where l3.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and l3.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey and l3.l_receiptdate > l3.l_commitdate ) and s_nationkey = n_nationkey and n_name = 'SAUDI ARABIA' group by s_name order by numwait desc, s_name limit 100;
rewritten_query:
SELECT s.s_name, COUNT(*) AS numwait
FROM supplier s
JOIN lineitem l1 ON s.s_suppkey = l1.l_suppkey
JOIN orders o ON o.o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey
JOIN nation n ON s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l2.l_suppkey) AS supplier_count,
           COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l2.l_receiptdate > l2.l_commitdate THEN l2.l_suppkey END) AS late_supplier_count
    FROM lineitem l2
    WHERE l2.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey
) stats
WHERE o.o_orderstatus = 'F'
  AND l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate
  AND n.n_name = 'SAUDI ARABIA'
  AND stats.supplier_count > 1
  AND stats.late_supplier_count = 1
GROUP BY s.s_name
ORDER BY numwait DESC, s.s_name
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated EXISTS (l2) and NOT EXISTS (l3) subqueries with a single LATERAL aggregate that computes, per candidate order, the number of distinct suppliers and the number of distinct suppliers with late lines. Conditions supplier_count > 1 and late_supplier_count = 1 are logically equivalent to the original EXISTS/NOT EXISTS pair given l1 is late: count>1 guarantees another supplier exists, and exactly one late supplier (which must be l1's supplier since l1 is late) guarantees no other supplier is late.

Convert implicit comma joins to explicit JOIN syntax and apply the LATERAL subquery only after the selective filters (SAUDI ARABIA nation, orderstatus 'F', l1 late) reduce l1 to roughly a few hundred thousand rows. Each LATERAL evaluation uses the lineitem primary-key index on l_orderkey, avoiding the massive hash anti join that builds a hash table over ~25M late lineitem rows.

Avoid the previous rewrite's MATERIALIZED CTEs, which forced a global aggregation/merge join over tens of millions of rows and caused a 5.3x cost regression. The LATERAL approach keeps the correlation local, allowing nested-loop + index-scan execution. Optionally, a covering index on lineitem(l_orderkey, l_receiptdate, l_commitdate, l_suppkey) would enable index-only scans in the LATERAL aggregate.

original_query: select s_name, count(*) as numwait from supplier, lineitem l1, orders, nation where s_suppkey = l1.l_suppkey and o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and o_orderstatus = 'F' and l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate and exists ( select * from lineitem l2 where l2.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and l2.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey ) and not exists ( select * from lineitem l3 where l3.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and l3.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey and l3.l_receiptdate > l3.l_commitdate ) and s_nationkey = n_nationkey and n_name = 'INDONESIA' group by s_name order by numwait desc, s_name limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH late_supplier AS (
    SELECT l_orderkey,
           l_suppkey,
           COUNT(*) AS late_cnt
    FROM lineitem
    WHERE l_receiptdate > l_commitdate
    GROUP BY l_orderkey, l_suppkey
),
sole_late_supplier AS (
    SELECT l_orderkey,
           MIN(l_suppkey) AS l_suppkey,
           SUM(late_cnt) AS late_cnt
    FROM late_supplier
    GROUP BY l_orderkey
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
)
SELECT s.s_name,
       CAST(SUM(sl.late_cnt) AS BIGINT) AS numwait
FROM sole_late_supplier sl
JOIN orders o
  ON o.o_orderkey = sl.l_orderkey
 AND o.o_orderstatus = 'F'
JOIN supplier s
  ON s.s_suppkey = sl.l_suppkey
JOIN nation n
  ON n.n_nationkey = s.s_nationkey
 AND n.n_name = 'INDONESIA'
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM lineitem l2
    WHERE l2.l_orderkey = sl.l_orderkey
      AND l2.l_suppkey <> sl.l_suppkey
)
GROUP BY s.s_name
ORDER BY numwait DESC, s.s_name
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated NOT EXISTS (l3) with a pre-aggregated CTE grouping late lineitems by (l_orderkey, l_suppkey), then keep only orders where HAVING COUNT(*) = 1, i.e., exactly one supplier has late lineitems. SUM(late_cnt) preserves the per-line count so results stay equivalent.
Rewrite comma-style joins as explicit JOINs and push the filters o_orderstatus = 'F' and n_name = 'INDONESIA' into the join conditions so candidate rows are reduced before the remaining EXISTS probe.

Keep the EXISTS (l2) as an indexed semi-join probe on lineitem(l_orderkey, l_suppkey) since 'another supplier exists' cannot be derived from the late-lineitems aggregate alone; evaluating it after the Indonesia/order-status filters reduces probe count.

Use COUNT(*) in late_supplier with SUM(late_cnt) in the final aggregation instead of joining raw lineitems, which avoids re-evaluating EXISTS/NOT EXISTS per late lineitem row (one evaluation per order/supplier group instead).

original_query: select cntrycode, count(*) as numcust, sum(c_acctbal) as totacctbal from ( select substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) as cntrycode, c_acctbal from customer where substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) in ('17', '22', '12', '18', '34', '25', '16') and c_acctbal > ( select avg(c_acctbal) from customer where c_acctbal > 0.00 and substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) in ('17', '22', '12', '18', '34', '25', '16') ) and not exists ( select * from orders where o_custkey = c_custkey ) ) as custsale group by cntrycode order by cntrycode;
rewritten_query:
WITH filtered_customers AS (
    SELECT
        c_custkey,
        c_acctbal,
        substring(c_phone FROM 1 FOR 2) AS cntrycode,
        avg(c_acctbal) OVER () AS avg_c_acctbal
    FROM customer
    WHERE c_acctbal > 0.00
      AND substring(c_phone FROM 1 FOR 2) IN ('17','22','12','18','34','25','16')
)
SELECT
    cntrycode,
    count(*) AS numcust,
    sum(c_acctbal) AS totacctbal
FROM filtered_customers fc
WHERE fc.c_acctbal > fc.avg_c_acctbal
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM orders o
      WHERE o.o_custkey = fc.c_custkey
  )
GROUP BY cntrycode
ORDER BY cntrycode;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the scalar avg subquery (which forces a second scan of customer) with a window function avg(c_acctbal) OVER () computed during the same filtered scan. Since avg of positive values is > 0, adding c_acctbal > 0.00 to the outer filter is provably equivalent to the original c_acctbal > avg condition.

The original outer query lacks c_acctbal > 0.00, but since avg over positive values is strictly positive, c_acctbal > avg implies c_acctbal > 0.00. Explicitly adding this predicate is safe and enables early filtering.
Compute substring(c_phone FROM 1 FOR 2) once as cntrycode in the CTE projection, avoiding repeated expression evaluation in outer SELECT and GROUP BY.

Keep NOT EXISTS (anti-join) as-is; it is already optimal for finding customers without orders. Do not rewrite to NOT IN (NULL semantics/performance issues). Recommend index on orders(o_custkey) to enable index-based anti-join instead of scanning all 15M orders.

original_query: select cntrycode, count(*) as numcust, sum(c_acctbal) as totacctbal from ( select substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) as cntrycode, c_acctbal from customer where substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) in ('24', '31', '26', '34', '30', '22', '14') and c_acctbal > ( select avg(c_acctbal) from customer where c_acctbal > 0.00 and substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) in ('24', '31', '26', '34', '30', '22', '14') ) and not exists ( select * from orders where o_custkey = c_custkey ) ) as custsale group by cntrycode order by cntrycode;
rewritten_query:
select cntrycode, count(*) as numcust, sum(c_acctbal) as totacctbal
from (
    select substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) as cntrycode, c_acctbal
    from customer
    where substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) in ('24', '31', '26', '34', '30', '22', '14')
      and c_acctbal > (
          select avg(c_acctbal)
          from customer
          where c_acctbal > 0.00
            and substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) in ('24', '31', '26', '34', '30', '22', '14')
      )
      and not exists (
          select 1
          from orders
          where o_custkey = c_custkey
      )
) as custsale
group by cntrycode
order by cntrycode;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The uncorrelated avg subquery is already executed once as an InitPlan by the optimizer, so converting it to a CTE or window function would not reduce work and could add materialization overhead. The dominant cost is the anti-join with orders (15M rows full scan). An index on orders(o_custkey) would convert the Parallel Hash Right Anti Join into an efficient Nested Loop Anti Join with index probes for the ~7k candidate customers. This is an index recommendation, not a SQL rewrite.
The repeated substring(c_phone from 1 for 2) expression could theoretically be hoisted via a CTE, but expression evaluation on 1.5M rows is negligible compared to the orders scan; no rewrite needed.
